diagnosis.headline: The payment container has been stopped since 10:27:50Z (exit 137, not OOM-killed). Every checkout fails because checkout can no longer resolve the payment hostname, and email has gone quiet because failed checkouts never reach the confirmation-email step.

root_causes.cause: The payment container exited at 2026-10-24T10:27:50Z with exit code 137 and has not restarted (restart_count 0). oom_killed=false, so this looks like an external SIGKILL or docker stop, not OOM. Once the container was gone, Docker DNS stopped resolving 'payment'. Checkout's Charge calls now fail with 'lookup payment on 127.0.0.11:53: server misbehaving' / 'produced zero addresses', so every checkout fails and the email step is never reached.

affected_services.impact: Container exited, so no Charge requests are served and its spans have stopped (silent).
100% of PlaceOrder requests fail at oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge with DNS resolver errors for 'payment'. p95 is 9500ms against a 6500ms baseline, and traffic has dropped.
No traffic, because checkout fails before sending the order confirmation. The container itself is running and healthy.
Users get errors when placing orders. Checkout calls take about 9.8s on average.

anomalies.observed: exited, exit code 137, oom_killed=false, stopped 189s ago (2026-10-24T10:27:50Z), health unhealthy

ruled_out.reason: The container is running and healthy, and it logged no warnings or errors. It is silent only because checkout fails at payment first.
The container is healthy. Its errors all come from the failed payment call (DNS for 'payment'), so checkout is a victim, not the origin.
Memory is at 93.36% of its limit, but it has not restarted, is healthy and is not flagged for errors. Its checkout failures pass through from checkout.

open_questions: What stopped payment with exit 137 when oom_killed=false? Check the docker daemon events and operator activity around 10:27:50Z.

Recommendation p95 rose to 4160ms (baseline 1981.2ms). Over the same window product-catalog p95 also rose, from 2365 to 4451ms, so this looks like a separate, milder slowdown that payment does not explain. Product-catalog / astronomy-db latency should be checked.
Frontend memory is at 93.36% of its 250MB limit. Watch it for growth or an OOM risk.
prevention: Set a restart policy (restart: unless-stopped/on-failure) on the payment container so it comes back automatically after an unexpected kill.
Alert directly on critical containers not running (exited status or a failing payment health check), so this fires before checkout errors pile up.
Audit who or what sends docker stop/kill to payment (exit 137, not OOM) and restrict manual container operations in this environment.

proposed_action.reason: The root cause is a stopped payment container. Restarting it brings back its DNS entry and its Charge endpoint for checkout.
proposed_action.risk_assessment: Low. The container is already down, so a restart cannot make things worse. If something external is deliberately killing it (exit 137 without OOM), it may stop again and a human will need to find out who or what stopped it.
proposed_action.expected_outcome: Payment spans come back at about the 0.057 rps baseline. Checkout error rate falls from 1.0 to about 0.0, email traffic returns to about 0.057 rps, and checkout p95 drops back toward the 6500ms baseline.

objections.text: The payment root cause holds up. The payment container exited (137, not OOM, 0 restarts), and all four error-trace classes end at checkout's PaymentService/Charge client span: DNS failure, zero addresses, no route to host and i/o timeout. The diagnosis cites only the two DNS traces, though. The 'no route to host' and 'i/o timeout' traces to 172.21.0.16 are left out, even though they fit the explanation and account for the higher checkout p95. This is a minor gap.

The diagnosis does not explain one alerting signal. Recommendation p95 rose from about 1.3s to 4.2s (peak 6.1s), and product-catalog p95 also rose from about 2.4s to 4.5s (peak 6.0s). Neither is in the payment→checkout→email chain. Neither appears in the root causes or the ruled-out list. Recommendation traffic is up, not down, so this cannot be a downstream effect of failed checkouts. It may be a second, separate fault, possibly product-catalog slowness spreading to recommendation, that this single-root-cause diagnosis misses. CPU data that could rule out resource pressure came back empty.

The memory pressure on opensearch (97.2% of limit) is not addressed. Log searches report 'opensearch (none)', so log-based negative evidence (no warn+ lines for checkout, email or payment) is weaker than it looks: the claim that email 'logged no warnings or errors' rests partly on a log backend that may be degraded.

alternative_root_cause.reason: The recommendation/product-catalog latency rise is not explained by the payment outage and may be a separate issue that needs its own investigation.
alternative_root_cause.note: shown to the human only; never acted on
